newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says safety of hostages top priority.
newsitem.headline: Japan says safety of hostages top priority.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Wednesday he has asked Peru to put high priority on the safety of the hostages held by guerrillas who stormed the residence of the Japanese ambassador to Peru.
"We want the safety of the hostages to be considered in their (the Peruvian authorities') handling of this case," Ikeda told a news conference.
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori put the number of hostages at 200 in a telephone conversation with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Fujimori said Interior Minister Juan Briones Davila was negotiating with the guerrillas for the release of the hostages.
The hostages include many high-ranking diplomats, business executives and academics attending a reception on Tuesday to honour the Japanese emperor's birthday.
Ikeda said all women and elderly people were freed.
The Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) threatened to kill the hostages unless the Peruvian government freed imprisoned fellow rebels.
"If they do not release our prisoners, we will all die in here," an MRTA spokesman told a local radio station from within the ambassador's residence.
Ikeda declined to comment on the guerrilla group's demands.
"I can't say anything at this stage about their demands," Ikeda said.

The rebels said they had 400 to 500 comrades in jail and that their highest priority was the release of Victor Polay, their leader who was imprisoned in 1992. They also called for a review of Peru's judicial system and direct negotiations with the government beginning at dawn on Wednesday.
